主要内容: Walgreens Boots Alliance reported its Q4 earnings, revealing that its shares fell on Thursday due to sales falling short of expectations. Excluding items, the company earned $1.48 per share, slightly above the $1.45 per share expected by analysts. However, sales were below the $33.78 billion analysts had anticipated. The company's revenue rose nearly 11% to $33.44 billion, driven by the acquisition of 1,932 Rite Aid stores. U.S. retail pharmacy sales increased to $25.5 billion, a 14.4% rise from the previous year. Same-store sales rose just 0.3%, with a 1.9% decline in the front-of-store sales, particularly in general merchandise and personal care. Walgreens is forecasting adjusted earnings per share to range from $6.40 to $6.70 for the next fiscal year. The company is also expanding partnerships with health insurers and LabCorp to enhance its services. The retail pharmacy sector is facing pressure from e-commerce giants like Amazon, which has further impacted traditional retail sales. Walgreens Boots Alliance, a major player in the retail sector, has been actively exploring new strategies to enhance its market position. In 2017, the company announced plans to partner with Birchbox, a digital beauty subscription company, to test a concept in a handful of Walgreens stores. This initiative allows shoppers to fill a kit with makeup, hair, and skincare samples, aiming to position Walgreens as a specialist in the beauty category and protect its business from competitors like Amazon. Additionally, Walgreens plans to test grocery pickups at its locations through a partnership with Kroger. The company's co-chief operating officer, Alex Gourlay, emphasized the importance of strategic partnerships, stating that Walgreens believes in collaborations that either accelerate its own work or bring capabilities it cannot easily develop. Gourlay noted that the transition to becoming a health, beauty, and wellness expert is well under way, though it may take longer than initially anticipated.
